correctness.rationale: Reflexive modules are second syzygies (Enomoto), and every second syzygy is projective for gl.dim A<=1, so ref A=proj A. For any simple right S, if projective it embeds as a direct summand of regular A and Hom(S,A)≠0. If nonprojective its minimal resolution 0→P1→P0→S→0 has nonzero projective P1; assuming Ext^1(S,A)=0 makes Hom(P0,A)→Hom(P1,A) surjective. Extending coordinates of a split embedding P1→A^m gives h:P0→A^m with hj equal to that embedding and a retraction P0→P1, which splits the resolution, contradiction. Hence each simple index belongs to I_ref(A), satisfying both hypotheses of Enomoto Theorem 5.5. Passage to basic Morita representative preserves heredity. This proves for all finite-dimensional hereditary k-algebras over arbitrary fields; no finite examples used as infinite proof.
